metadata.title: Explanation of Machine Learning Models of Colon Cancer Using SHAP Considering Interaction Effects

extraction_notes.note: The source joins 'can be calculated ... black box,' and the uniqueness statement with a comma instead of a period, so the theorem span must start at the black-box sentence.
theorem (external) or claim: the GLM ranking equivalence is stated without citation right after the cited importance definition, read as the cited paper's result.
Empirical findings read off SHAP plots and a table were emitted as claims with rigor numerical; descriptive text about the cohort, plot conventions and the AUC was not extracted.

Introduction, Experiments preamble and Conclusion restate the Shapley-Taylor method and the bilirubin finding; restated copies got no node, as did the closing 'Therefore, high bilirubin levels...' sentence that repeats ClP8.

These nodes end with a displayed formula that has no closing period, followed by a new capitalised sentence; the finishing step warns 'ends mid-sentence', but extending them would merge separate definitions, so the spans end at the display.
Several findings exist only as figures and a table (Table importance_top10, SHAP dependence plots); the nodes quote the prose that reports them.

nodes.name: SHAP compatibility with linear models
nodes.statement: SHAP is also highly compatible with linear models and the derivative of the SHAP value corresponds to the regression coefficient of the linear model.
conclusions: SHAP is also highly compatible with linear models and the derivative of the SHAP value corresponds to the regression coefficient of the linear model

nodes.name: Interaction effect
nodes.statement: An interaction effect occurs when the impact of one feature depends on another feature.
differentia: the impact of one feature depends on another feature

nodes.name: Potassium supplements and ACE inhibitors drug interaction
nodes.statement: For example, potassium supplements and ACE inhibitors are safe alone; however, their combined use can cause hyperkalemia by drug interaction.

nodes.name: SHapley Additive exPlanation (SHAP)
nodes.statement: \textit{SHapley Additive exPlanation} (SHAP)~\cite{lundberg2017unified} is a method for interpreting the results of machine learning by computing the contribution of each feature and represents the outcome of patient-$j$: $f(x^{(j)})$ as the sum of each features-$i$'s contribution $\phi_i(x_i^{(j)})$. \begin{equation} f(x^{(j)})=\phi_0+\sum_{i=1}^{K} \phi_i(x_i^{(j)}) \end{equation} \begin{equation} \phi_0=\frac{1}{N} \sum_{j=1}^{N} f(x^{(j)}) \end{equation} \begin{equation} \phi_i(x_i^{(j)})=\Phi(x_i^{(j)}) - \frac{1}{N} \sum_{k=1}^{N} \Phi({x_i}^{(k)}) \end{equation} , where $N$ is the number of patients and $\Phi(x_i)$ is the Shapley value for $x_i$.
nodes.genus: a method for interpreting the results of machine learning
differentia: by computing the contribution of each feature
represents the outcome of patient-$j$: $f(x^{(j)})$ as the sum of each features-$i$'s contribution $\phi_i(x_i^{(j)})$
nodes.statement_short: SHAP writes a model output as a baseline (mean prediction) plus per-feature contributions, each a centred Shapley value.

nodes.name: Shapley value
nodes.statement: The Shapley value is a fair profit allocation among many stakeholders depending on their contribution~\cite{roth1988shapley} and was derived from the name of the economist who introduced it. The Shapley value is defined as follows: \begin{multline} \Phi(x_i) \\ =\sum_{S \subseteq \{1,\cdots,K\} \setminus \{i\}} \frac{|S|!(K-|S|-1)!}{K!}[f_{x}(S\cup\{i\})-f_{x}(S)] \end{multline} , where $K$ is the number of stakeholders or features.
nodes.genus: a fair profit allocation among many stakeholders
nodes.statement_short: Shapley value of player $i$: weighted average over coalitions $S$ of the marginal gain $f_x(S\cup\{i\})-f_x(S)$.

nodes.name: Shapley value formula
nodes.statement: \Phi(x_i) \\ =\sum_{S \subseteq \{1,\cdots,K\} \setminus \{i\}} \frac{|S|!(K-|S|-1)!}{K!}[f_{x}(S\cup\{i\})-f_{x}(S)]
nodes.label: SHAPdef

nodes.name: Marginal contribution
nodes.statement: The meaning of the bracket part of Eq.~(\ref{SHAPdef}) is that the contribution of entity-$i$ can be defined as a marginal contribution, i.e. the difference between the profit obtained by group-$S$ members only: $f_{x}(S)$ and that of both entity-$i$ and the group members: $f_{x}(S\cup\{i\})$.
nodes.statement_short: The bracket in the Shapley formula is the marginal contribution of $i$: coalition value $f_x(S\cup\{i\})$ minus $f_x(S)$.

nodes.name: Uniqueness of the Shapley value
nodes.statement: The Shapley values can be calculated as long as the function value is defined even if the calculation method is a black box, The Shapley value is the only profit allocation method that satisfies the following four properties: efficiency, symmetry, linearity, and null player.
conclusions: The Shapley value is the only profit allocation method that satisfies the following four properties: efficiency, symmetry, linearity, and null player
nodes.statement_short: Shapley values need only black-box function evaluations, and are the unique allocation satisfying efficiency, symmetry, linearity and null player.

nodes.name: Polynomial-time SHAP for tree ensembles (TreeSHAP)
nodes.statement: The computation time of naive SHAP calculations increases exponentially with the number of features $K$; however, Lundberg et al. proposed a polynomial-time algorithm for decision trees and ensemble trees model~\cite{lundberg2020local}.

nodes.name: SHAP variable importance
nodes.statement: Notara et al. proposed using the variance (L2-norm) of the SHAP value for measuring variable importance~\cite{nohara2022shap}.
nodes.genus: the variance (L2-norm) of the SHAP value

nodes.name: Equivalence of SHAP importance ranking and GLM coefficient ranking
nodes.statement: The ranking result sorted by the absolute value of the beta coefficients $\beta_i$ in the generalized linear regression model is exactly the same as that of this definition.
conclusions: The ranking result sorted by the absolute value of the beta coefficients $\beta_i$ in the generalized linear regression model is exactly the same as that of this definition
nodes.statement_short: For a generalized linear model, ranking features by SHAP variance coincides with ranking by $|\beta_i|$.

nodes.name: Three-variable function with main effect and interaction terms
nodes.statement: In order to understand what the SHAP value means, we suppose the three-variable function $F(x,y,z)$ is expressed as the following equation. \begin{equation} F(x,y,z)=f_x(x)+f_y(y)+f_z(z)+g_{xy}(x,y)+g_{xz}(x,z) \end{equation} , where $f(x)$ is the main effect term for the feature $x$ and $g(x,y)$ is the interaction term of features $x$ and $y$.
nodes.statement_short: Toy model $F$ = sum of main effect terms $f_x,f_y,f_z$ plus interaction terms $g_{xy},g_{xz}$.

nodes.name: Three-variable test function
nodes.statement: F(x,y,z)=f_x(x)+f_y(y)+f_z(z)+g_{xy}(x,y)+g_{xz}(x,z)
nodes.label: 3value

nodes.name: SHAP values of the three-variable function
nodes.statement: The respective contributions of each feature $x$, $y$, and $z$ in this function are as follows: $$\phi(x)=f_x(x)+\frac{g_{xy}(x,y)+g_{xz}(x,z)}{2}$$ $$\phi(y)=f_y(y)+\frac{g_{xy}(x,y)}{2}$$ $$\phi(z)=f_z(z)+\frac{g_{xz}(x,z)}{2}$$ $$F(x,y,z)=\phi(x)+\phi(y)+\phi(z)$$
nodes.statement_short: On $F$, each feature's SHAP value is its main effect plus half of each interaction it is involved in.

nodes.name: SHAP cannot separate main effects from interactions
nodes.statement: In other words, the SHAP value of the feature evaluates the sum of the main effect term of the feature and the interactions between the feature and others. Therefore, we can evaluate which features are important; however, we cannot distinguish whether the main effect term is affecting the outcome or interactions are affecting the outcome.
nodes.statement_short: A SHAP value mixes a feature's main effect with its interactions, so it ranks importance but cannot tell the two apart.

nodes.name: Shapley-Taylor index
nodes.statement: The Shapley-Taylor index is an extended version of the Shapley value~\cite{sundararajan2020shapley} and decomposes the SHAP value $\Phi(x_i) $ into the main term $\Phi(x_i,x_i)$ and interaction terms $\Phi(x_i,x_j)$ as the following equation: $$\Phi(x_i)=\Phi(x_i,x_i)+\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j\neq i}\Phi(x_i,x_j)$$
nodes.genus: an extended version of the Shapley value
differentia: decomposes the SHAP value $\Phi(x_i) $ into the main term $\Phi(x_i,x_i)$ and interaction terms $\Phi(x_i,x_j)$
nodes.statement_short: The Shapley-Taylor index splits $\Phi(x_i)$ into a main term $\Phi(x_i,x_i)$ plus half the sum of pairwise interaction terms.

nodes.name: Shapley-Taylor interaction effect term
nodes.statement: An interaction effect terms $\Phi(x_i,x_j)$ is defined as follows: \begin{multline} \Phi(x_i,x_j) \\ = \sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\cdots,K\}/\{i,j\}} \frac{2\cdot|S|!(K-|S|-1)!}{K!} [f_x(S\cup\{i,j\}) \\ - f_x(S\cup\{i\})-f_x(S\cup\{j\})+f_x(S)] \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Pairwise interaction term: weighted sum over coalitions of the discrete second difference of $f_x$ in $i$ and $j$.

nodes.name: Shapley-Taylor interaction term formula
nodes.statement: \Phi(x_i,x_j) \\ = \sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\cdots,K\}/\{i,j\}} \frac{2\cdot|S|!(K-|S|-1)!}{K!} [f_x(S\cup\{i,j\}) \\ - f_x(S\cup\{i\})-f_x(S\cup\{j\})+f_x(S)]

nodes.name: Shapley-Taylor main effect term
nodes.statement: A main effect terms $\Phi(x_i,x_i)$ is defined using the interaction terms $\Phi(x_i,x_j)$ and the Shapley values $\Phi(x_i)$. $$\Phi(x_i,x_i)=\ \Phi(x_i)-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j\neq i}\Phi(x_i,x_j)$$
nodes.statement_short: Main effect term = Shapley value minus half the sum of its pairwise interaction terms.

nodes.name: Shapley-Taylor index on the three-variable function
nodes.statement: Using the Shapley-Taylor index, the three-variable function $F(x,y,z)$ in Eq.~\ref{3value} is evaluated as $\Phi_{x,x}=f(x)$, $\Phi_{x,y}=g(x,y)$ and $\Phi_{x,z}=g(x,z)$. The Shapley-Taylor index enables to evaluate the effect of the main effect term and the interaction terms separately.
nodes.statement_short: On $F$ the Shapley-Taylor index recovers the main effect $f(x)$ and the interactions $g(x,y)$, $g(x,z)$ exactly.

nodes.name: Shapley interaction value versus Shapley-Taylor index
nodes.statement_short: Unlike the Shapley-Taylor index, the Shapley interaction value does not recover the main effect and interaction terms of $F$.

nodes.name: Cox proportional hazards model with GBDT baseline hazard analysed by SHAP
nodes.statement: A survival time analysis using the Cox proportional hazards model was conducted with the seven baseline characteristics as features and the development of colon cancer as the outcome. In general, logistic regression is often applied as the baseline hazard function in the Cox proportional hazards model; however, the Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT), a typical machine learning model method, was applied in this analysis. The baseline hazard function generated by the GBDT is analyzed by SHAP to determine what combination of baseline characteristics contributes to the development of colon cancer.
input: the seven baseline characteristics as features
the development of colon cancer as the outcome
nodes.statement_short: Fit a Cox survival model whose baseline hazard is a gradient boosting decision tree, then explain it with SHAP.

nodes.name: Bilirubin threshold 1.2 mg/dl for colon cancer risk
nodes.statement: Figure~\ref{sdp_all} is a SHAP dependence plots for colon cancer risk against serum bilirubin levels and shows the SHAP value decreases significantly when bilirubin is larger than 1.2 mg/dl. This indicates that bilirubin 1.2 mg/dl is the threshold for decreasing the risk of developing colon cancer.
conclusions: the SHAP value decreases significantly when bilirubin is larger than 1.2 mg/dl
bilirubin 1.2 mg/dl is the threshold for decreasing the risk of developing colon cancer

nodes.name: Antioxidant explanation of bilirubin effect
nodes.statement: One of the possible causes is as follows. Cancer-associated infections, smoking, obesity, diabetes, ionizing and ultraviolet radiation, and air pollution are established risk factors for cancer development. All of these factors are likely to be associated with increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) production in humans. Increased ROS production has been hypothesized to damage DNA, proteins, and lipids, and thus initiate or promote cancer development. Since bilirubin is a strong endogenous antioxidant, higher serum bilirubin levels reduce the cancer risk through decreasing of ROS production~\cite{inoguchi2021association}.
nodes.statement_short: Hypothesised mechanism: bilirubin is an antioxidant, so higher levels lower ROS production and hence cancer risk.

nodes.name: Spread of SHAP values attributed to interactions
nodes.statement: In the SHAP Dependence Plot in Figure~\ref{shap_summary}, SHAP values are distributed widely for the same bilirubin value (e.g., SHAP values are distributed widely from -0.4 to -0.2 when bilirubin is 1.2). This is caused by an interaction between bilirubin and other features.
conclusions: This is caused by an interaction between bilirubin and other features

nodes.name: Main-effect importance ranking of colon cancer risk factors
nodes.statement: If we focus only on the main effect of features, the important features are age, bilirubin, triglycerides, BMI, and smoking history, in descending order. This result is consistent with the ranking of the existing method in Figure~\ref{shap_summary}.
assumptions: If we focus only on the main effect of features
conclusions: the important features are age, bilirubin, triglycerides, BMI, and smoking history, in descending order

nodes.name: Main effect of bilirubin removes spread of SHAP values
nodes.statement: Figure~\ref{sdp_single} is a SHAP dependence plot for colon cancer risk evaluating the main effect of serum bilirubin levels and shows the SHAP value decreases significantly when bilirubin is larger than 1.2 mg/dl. This shape is very similar to SHAP Dependence Plot in Figure~\ref{sdp_all}; however, SHAP values are not distributed widely for the same bilirubin value (e.g., all SHAP values are almost -0.3 when bilirubin is 1.2). This is caused by eliminating the interaction between bilirubin and other features from the SHAP value of bilirubin.
nodes.statement_short: The bilirubin main effect keeps the 1.2 mg/dl drop but loses the vertical spread, which therefore came from interactions.

nodes.name: Bilirubin-age interaction effect
nodes.statement: Figure~\ref{sdp_age} shows the SHAP dependence plots evaluating the interaction effect of serum bilirubin levels and ages. In the group of 20s, we found the interaction effect rises significantly when bilirubin exceeds 1.2 mg/dl, while those in their 50s and 60s show a slight decrease in the interaction value when bilirubin exceeds 1.2 mg/dl.

nodes.name: Main plus interaction effect of bilirubin by age
nodes.statement: Figure~\ref{sdp_age_sum} shows the SHAP dependence plots evaluating the main and interaction effects of serum bilirubin levels and ages. For the 20s, when bilirubin exceeds 1.2 mg/dl, the decrease in the main effect of bilirubin cancels out the increase in the interaction effect, and the sum of their SHAP values does not change significantly. On the other hand, for the 30s and older, the decrease in the main effect of bilirubin outweighed the increase in the interaction effect, and the sum of their SHAP values decreased when bilirubin exceeds 1.2 mg/dl.
nodes.statement_short: For people in their 20s the bilirubin main-effect drop is cancelled by the interaction rise; from the 30s on, the total SHAP value decreases.

nodes.name: High bilirubin lowers colon cancer risk especially for the elderly
nodes.statement: Since the interaction effect is getting smaller with older age, high bilirubin levels decrease the risk of colon cancer, especially for the elderly.
assumptions: Since the interaction effect is getting smaller with older age
conclusions: high bilirubin levels decrease the risk of colon cancer, especially for the elderly

nodes.name: Justification of the age-dependent bilirubin effect
nodes.statement: This is because there is much room for risk reduction for the elderly since their risk is larger than that of the young generation.
nodes.statement_short: Direct argument: the elderly have higher baseline risk, so there is more room for risk reduction.
